scenes.title: WHY THE SKY IS BLUE
scenes.subtitle: The color starts with white sunlight.
scenes.narration: Sunlight looks white, but it is a mixture of all the colors we can see.

scenes.title: LIGHT MEETS AIR
scenes.subtitle: Tiny molecules redirect incoming light.
scenes.narration: In the atmosphere, small molecules scatter short blue wavelengths much more strongly than longer red wavelengths.

scenes.title: BLUE FROM EVERYWHERE
scenes.subtitle: Scattered blue light fills the sky.
scenes.narration: That blue light spreads in every direction and reaches our eyes from across the sky above us.
beats: Blue photons scatter in the air
Our eyes see a sky-wide blue glow

scenes.title: BUT WHY NOT VIOLET?
scenes.subtitle: Our vision favors the blue we notice.
scenes.narration: Violet scatters even more, but sunlight has less of it, and our eyes respond less strongly.
beats: The spectrum and our eyes also matter
Together, we perceive a blue sky

scenes.title: THE SUNSET TWIST
scenes.subtitle: Longer paths reveal warmer colors.
scenes.narration: At sunset, sunlight travels through more air. More blue scatters away, leaving brilliant orange and red colors.
